::: {#rem-surprisal-fisher-information}
#### Surprisal and the Fisher information

When the probabilities depend on a parameter $\param$,
the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of an outcome $x$ is $-\log \p(x \mid \param)$,
which is minus the log-likelihood:

$$\surprisal_{\param}(x) = -\log \p(x \mid \param) = -\llik(\param).$$

Its derivative with respect to $\param$ is minus the
[score](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-score):

$$\deriv{\param} \surprisal_{\param}(x) = -\scoref{\param}.$$

The expected squared score is the
[expected information](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-einf),
also called the Fisher information.
It is also the expected
[second derivative](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-derivatives.html#def-second-derivative)
of the surprisal,
when $x$ is drawn from the model at the true parameter value $\param_0$
and both are taken under that value:

$$
\einf(\param_0)
= \Expp_{\param_0}\sb{\scoref{\param_0}^2}
= \Expp_{\param_0}\sb{\evalAt{\dderiv{\param} \surprisal_{\param}(x)}{\param = \param_0}}.
$$

It is also the second derivative, at the true parameter value,
of the [Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence)
between the model at that value and the model at the varying value
([proved in the sds notes](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#thm-fisher-kl-curvature)):

$$\evalAt{\dderiv{\param} \kldivf{\param_0}{\param}}{\param = \param_0} = \einf(\param_0).$$

:::
